_README: TEMPLATE + WORKED DRAFT for data/cases.json — the case library the agent
grounds its triage in. Copy an entry into data/cases.json once it is correct.
SCHEMA CHANGES vs the noc-ai-lab library (all additive; old cases still load):
escalate_to           replaces free-prose `escalation` with real Slack IDs and
ticket refs. The agent can only @mention what it is given;
prose like 'the edge platform team' is unmentionable, which
is why real runs keep ending in 'someone confirm the handle'.
discriminating_check  the single test that separates KNOWN from NEW. This is the
highest-value field in the whole file — see the engine
failure draft below. Without it the agent re-derives a
diagnosis every time for a condition the team already knows.
known_issues          open tickets this alert is currently explained by, each with
the condition under which that explanation applies.
auto_resolves         does it clear on its own, and how fast? Drives whether the
agent should open a thread at all.
evidence_to_post      what a human actually attaches. Tells the agent which
deterministic evidence matters for THIS alert type — e.g.
engine failure is Edge UI, not Grafana.
DO NOT SANITIZE. The noc-ai-lab library used <IP>/<cluster>/<instance-id>
placeholders because it was a pre-approval shadow project on a personal Slack.
This repo already holds production Edge tokens and reads the real channels, so a
placeholder is pure loss: '<IP>' cannot be run, compared, or escalated on.
WHAT MAKES A CASE GOOD: the gotchas. 'reboot, don't restart nfs-server — D-state
processes never clear' is worth more than ten diagnosis steps, because it is the
thing no runbook says and every engineer learns the hard way.
_PRIORITY: Ranked by (how often it fires) x (how badly the agent handles it today).
1. Engine failure rate above 15%   MOST FREQUENT VictorOps incident, fully
automated by this repo, and COMPLETELY ABSENT from the library. Draft below.
2. KubePodNotReady                 fires on prod1001; only KubePodsNotReady covered
3. AlbUnhealthyHostWarning         the Warning tier; only Critical covered
PandoLogic; only the Critical disk case is covered
5. Standard Apps Smoke Test UNSTABLE   Jenkins, 2-hourly
6. Docusign Platform / other synthetic 'X Platform' probes
VM ActiveRedAlarms and DiskSpaceUtilizationCritical are all thin (2-3 steps, 1
observed occurrence, no example_commands on some).

cases.environment: all aiWARE clusters; observed on aiw-prd5001, aiw-prod1001, aiw-dmh1001
cases.auto_resolves: Almost always. RESOLVED_BY: SYSTEM, usually within ~35 min. On prd5001 it pages roughly every 2 hours around the clock — every one ACKed and auto-resolved with no action possible (Shital Patel, 24 Aug).
cases.discriminating_check: Pull the failed tasks in Edge UI and read their CREATION DATES. Old dates (the same stuck batch) = known, no action. Recent dates = something new, investigate properly. Shital Patel stated this explicitly on 19 Aug: '1,872 tasks across prod1001/dmh1001/prd5001 (all created 14-16 Aug) are stuck retrying, so this will keep re-firing until they're cleared - if a future alert has *recent* task dates instead, that's something new and worth investigating.'

known_issues.applies_when: Error Type is `unknown` and the engine is Output Writer
known_issues.summary: Core writes some jobs/tasks to the parent table instead of the weekly partition, so Output Writer cannot upload results and tasks fail with error type `unknown`.

known_issues.applies_when: Output Writer reports `unknown` rather than a real error
known_issues.summary: Output Writer should fail fast on not_found from Core GraphQL uploadEngineResult instead of reprocessing into an unknown failure.
69 stations fail 100% on WideOrbit status-poll timeout.

known_issues.applies_when: Engine is SI2 Playback segment creator on aiw-prd5001
known_issues.summary: Introduced by PR #10693; revert merged as PR #10709 (2470d8ae0) but NOT yet deployed to prd5001. Needs realtime/v3.80.4.7386 or later — 3.80.4.7385 still has the bug, so the check is >= 72386.

diagnosis_steps: Edge UI -> Processing -> Tasks, filter to the engine and the alert's window. Record total / completed / failed and the percentages.
Identify the failing engine by name AND id; post both.
Open a failed task's detail for the error TYPE (unknown / bad_data / internal_error) and the raw failureDetail.
Record the affected org id and the TDO.
Check the failed tasks' creation dates — see discriminating_check.
Download the task and job logs and attach them.
resolution_steps: There is usually nothing for the NOC to fix — the fix is a code change or a deploy owned by another team.
Match the error type against known_issues and name the ticket in the thread.
If it matches a known issue with the stuck-batch signature, say so and let it auto-resolve.
If task dates are recent or the error type is new, escalate with engine id, org, TDO, error type and logs.
gotchas: The percentage in the alert and the percentage you capture will often disagree, because the alert evaluated its own window and you are looking at now. Say which window you measured; do not silently reconcile them.
`bad_data` points at the source media for that TDO, not at the engine host — do not escalate it as an infra problem.
Error Type `unknown` is the VE-23618 signature, not an absence of information.
This alert pages ~12x/day on prd5001 alone. Every fire is ACKed and auto-resolves. Do not treat a fresh page as evidence of a fresh problem.
A revert being merged does NOT mean it is deployed to the affected cluster — check the running version (VE-26837 was merged and still firing days later).
evidence_to_post: Edge UI Tasks page, filtered to engine + window (screenshot)
Edge UI Engine page, same filter (screenshot)
NOT Grafana — this is an Edge UI investigation
